title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 116: The Art and Mystery of Chinese Sericulture
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 116 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

The Art and Mystery of Chinese Sericulture

Paragraph 1. For over two thousand years, China kept the secret of making real silk. According to an old Chinese story, around 2700 BCE, Empress Leizu was drinking hot tea under a white mulberry tree. Suddenly, a silkworm cocoon fell into her warm cup. When she pulled it out, the heat softened the sticky coating, and one shiny thread began to unwind. Soon, she taught people how to raise silkworms and weave soft silk cloth.

Paragraph 2. Over centuries, Chinese farmers changed wild silkmoths into gentle farm insects. Today, adult farm silkmoths are completely blind, cannot fly, and cannot eat. They live only a few days to lay eggs before dying. Young silkworms are very delicate and eat only fresh leaves from the white mulberry tree. After eating for weeks, each worm spins a tight white cocoon around itself using liquid protein from its mouth.

Paragraph 3. To collect unbroken silk threads, workers must act before the adult moth bites its way out. If a moth breaks the cocoon, one long 900-metre thread gets cut into useless short pieces. Therefore, workers drop whole cocoons into boiling water. This kills the insect inside and melts the sticky natural glue, so workers can gently pull out the long thread and twist several threads together.

Paragraph 4. In old China, rolls of silk were even used as money to pay soldiers and government workers. Strict rules said only the Emperor could wear bright yellow silk clothing, and anyone caught stealing silkworm eggs out of China was killed. Silk travelled along the famous Silk Road to Rome, where rich buyers spent huge amounts of gold. Finally, in 552 CE, Roman Emperor Justinian sent two monks to China. They hid live silkworm eggs inside hollow bamboo walking sticks and brought them safely back, ending China's secret.

groups.title: Questions 5–8
groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information in the passage? Write TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

steps: Đoạn 1: "...Empress Leizu was drinking hot tea... cocoon fell into her warm cup."
Đoạn 2: "...eat only fresh leaves from the white mulberry tree."

q5.text: Domesticated adult silkmoths can fly long distances to find food.

steps: Đoạn 2: Bướm tằm nuôi bị mù, không thể bay và không thể ăn (cannot fly, and cannot eat).

q6.text: Workers boil cocoons to prevent the long silk thread from being cut into pieces.

steps: Đoạn 3: Nếu để bướm cắn chui ra sợi tơ sẽ bị đứt thành mảnh nhỏ vô dụng, nên phải nhúng kén vào nước sôi trước.

q7.text: In old China, ordinary people were allowed to wear bright yellow silk clothing.

steps: Đoạn 4: Chỉ Hoàng đế mới được mặc lụa màu vàng tươi (only the Emperor).

q8.text: Emperor Justinian gave the two monks special maps for their journey to China.

steps: Đoạn 4: Bài chỉ nói Hoàng đế sai hai tu sĩ đi, không nhắc việc tặng bản đồ.
